title: Kerala Road Trip: Hills, Backwaters and Coast by Road
seoTitle: Kerala Road Trip: Hills, Backwaters and Coast by Road
metaDescription: A Kerala road trip: Kochi to Munnar, Thekkady, Vagamon, Alappuzha and Varkala, with Wayanad in the north, drive times, a 7 to 10 day plan and seasons.
description: A route guide to a Kerala road trip: the classic loop from Kochi to Munnar, Thekkady, Vagamon, Kumarakom or Alappuzha and Varkala, the northern leg to Wayanad over the Thamarassery ghat, approximate distances and drive times, NH66 works, monsoon driving, a seven- to ten-day plan and how to combine driving with a houseboat night.
dek: Kerala's roads climb from the coast to tea hills and spice country, then drop back to backwaters and cliffs within a week.

hero.alt: A road through the tea estates of Munnar, Kerala

intro: Kerala is a narrow state, so its road trips are short in distance but slow in time: the drive from Kochi to Munnar is only about 130 km but takes four to five hours. The classic loop starts in Kochi, climbs to Munnar, crosses the Cardamom Hills to Thekkady, drops through Vagamon or Kottayam to the backwaters at Kumarakom or Alappuzha, and follows the coast south to Varkala. Wayanad, in the north, is a separate leg from Kozhikode.
NH66, the west-coast highway, is being widened to six lanes; many sections are complete, but works still slow traffic in places.
quickAnswer: The classic Kerala road trip runs Kochi–Munnar (about 130 km)–Thekkady (about 90 km)–Kumarakom or Alappuzha (about 140 km)–Varkala (about 140 km), over 7 to 10 days, with a night on a houseboat or by the backwaters. Wayanad can be added from Kozhikode via the Thamarassery ghat. October to March is best; the monsoon is beautiful but brings landslides on hill roads.
takeaways: Distances are short but hill roads are slow; plan three to five hours per leg.
Munnar and Thekkady need two nights each to enjoy them.
A houseboat is not a road trip; park the car at the jetty for a night.
NH66 widening is largely complete but works remain in places.
Follow district alerts in the monsoon; hill roads can close for landslides.

sections.heading: The northern leg: Wayanad
paras: Wayanad sits on a plateau reached from Kozhikode over the Thamarassery ghat, with nine hairpin bends. It combines well with Coorg or Mysuru across the Karnataka border, or with the northern beaches at Kannur and Bekal. Parts of Wayanad suffered deadly landslides in July 2024; follow district alerts in the monsoon.

sections.heading: Driving considerations
list: Roads are narrow and busy with buses; overtake only with clear sight lines.
Hill roads have many hairpins and fog in the mornings; drive in daylight.
Parking is scarce in Fort Kochi and Munnar town; use hotel parking.
Toll plazas on NH66 and NH544 accept FASTag.

sections.heading: Worth stopping for
list: Thattekad bird sanctuary near Kothamangalam, on the way to Munnar.
The spice plantations and viewpoints around Bodimettu on the Munnar–Thekkady road.
Vagamon's meadows and pine plantation between Thekkady and the backwaters.
Kottayam's old churches and the lakeside at Kumarakom.
Alappuzha beach and the canals at dusk.
Jatayu Earth's Center near Chadayamangalam, if you take the inland route south.

sections.heading: Food on the road
paras: Toddy-shop style kitchens serve karimeen (pearl spot), tapioca and fish curry around the backwaters, and highway cafés in the hills serve appam, puttu and parotta with curries. In Munnar and Thekkady, look for fresh cardamom tea and spice-garden lunches.

sections.heading: When to go
paras: October to March is best, with clear hills and calm backwaters. April and May are hot on the coast but pleasant in Munnar. The south-west monsoon (June to September) brings heavy rain; the hills are at their greenest, but landslides can close roads, and some viewpoints shut on red-alert days.

safety: Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road status and weather updates each morning and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, tolls, entry fees, pass openings and road works change; check official sources shortly before you travel.
Distances and driving times are approximate and vary with traffic, weather, road works and stops.
packing: Driving licence, RC, insurance and PUC certificate, with copies
Warm layers and a rain jacket
Cash for small towns and barriers

faqs.q: What is the best route for a Kerala road trip?
faqs.a: Kochi–Munnar–Thekkady–Alappuzha or Kumarakom–Varkala, over seven to ten days.

faqs.q: How long does it take to drive from Kochi to Munnar?
faqs.a: Usually four to five hours for about 130 km.

faqs.q: Can I combine a houseboat with a road trip?
faqs.a: Yes. Park at the jetty in Alappuzha or Kumarakom and spend a night on the water.

faqs.q: Is it safe to drive in Kerala in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Main roads stay open, but hill roads can close for landslides. Follow district alerts.

faqs.q: How many days do I need?
faqs.a: Seven days for the classic loop; ten with Wayanad or Varkala.
It is possible, but many visitors hire a car with a driver because of busy, narrow roads.
